facts.fact: AdWave states that midterm primary turnout typically runs 15-30% of registered voters, and far less in many local races.
facts.quote: Midterm primary turnout typically runs 15-30% of registered voters, and in many local races far less.

facts.fact: AdWave says typical CTV rates are $15-35 CPM.
facts.quote: at typical CTV rates of $15-35 CPM

facts.fact: AdWave recommends that the final two weeks of a primary TV effort hold 40-50% of the total TV budget.
facts.quote: This is where 40-50% of your total TV budget belongs.

facts.fact: AdWave recommends an effective primary TV effort run 6-8 weeks, back-weighted toward election day.
facts.quote: An effective primary TV effort is a 6-8 week campaign, back-weighted toward election day.

facts.fact: AdWave's illustrative example allocates $15,000 to an 8-week down-ballot primary TV effort, with $2,500 (about 17%) in weeks 8-6, $5,000 (about 33%) in weeks 5-3, and $7,500 (about 50%) in the final 2 weeks.
facts.quote: A practical allocation for a down-ballot campaign putting $15,000 into an 8-week primary TV effort:

facts.fact: AdWave claims that in open-seat primaries with three or more candidates, races are routinely won with 30-40% of the vote.
facts.quote: races are routinely won with 30-40% of the vote

facts.fact: AdWave recommends weighting primary CTV delivery toward households aged 45 and over in high-turnout precincts.
facts.quote: Weighting delivery toward 45+ households in high-turnout precincts concentrates impressions where primary votes live

facts.fact: AdWave recommends that primary spots put the candidate's name on screen for the full 30 seconds.
facts.quote: put the name on screen for the full 30 seconds

facts.fact: Adwave states that it generates a broadcast-quality 30-second spot from a campaign website in about two minutes.
facts.quote: Adwave generates a broadcast-quality 30-second spot from a campaign website in about two minutes

facts.fact: Adwave states that a campaign can be live on 100+ networks in under ten minutes once verified.
facts.quote: a campaign can be live on 100+ networks in under ten minutes once verified

facts.fact: The page says meaningful local primary CTV programs start around $2,000-$5,000 for a focused final month.
facts.quote: Meaningful local programs start around $2,000-$5,000 for a focused final month

facts.fact: The page says competitive legislative or countywide races commonly invest $10,000-$30,000 in CTV across the full window.
facts.quote: competitive legislative or countywide races commonly invest $10,000-$30,000 across the full window

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping roughly half of the TV budget for the final two weeks.
facts.quote: keep roughly half your TV budget for the final two weeks, whatever your total is

facts.fact: The page states that broadcast advertising pays for the whole market, including the 70-85% of adults who won't vote in the campaign's primary.
facts.quote: including the 70-85% of adults who won't vote in your primary and everyone outside your district

facts.fact: The page recommends starting TV advertising six to eight weeks before ballots are cast for most down-ballot primaries.
facts.quote: Six to eight weeks before ballots are cast is the practical sweet spot for most down-ballot primaries

facts.fact: The page advises starting platform political-advertiser verification 3-5 days before launch.
facts.quote: Platform political-advertiser verification | 3-5 days before launch

facts.fact: The page says that a few states regulate windows and rates for political ads.
facts.quote: A few states regulate windows and rates

facts.fact: The page says a six-week primary window does not allow clean attribution, but useful signal can be obtained.
facts.quote: You won't get clean attribution inside a six-week window
